Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ONE production sprite atlas for a monochrome e-ink RPG. Use reference 1 as the exact male hero style/proportion and reference 2 as the exact female heroine style/proportion. Create a transparent square sprite-sheet atlas, ideally 2048 x 2048, with EXACTLY 5 equal columns and 4 equal rows = 20 COMPLETE characters, one centered inside each equal rectangular cell. No drawn grid, text, labels, numbers, backgrounds or shadows. Every figure must fit well inside its cell with transparent margins, with no wings, hair or feet spilling into adjacent cells.
Grid order is CRITICAL: row 1 = male costumes A-E; row 2 = female versions of the SAME costumes A-E; row 3 = male costumes F-J; row 4 = female versions of the SAME costumes F-J. Match each costume's silhouette and details across its male/female pair. All are COMPLETE connected characters, from hair to boots, NEVER torso pieces or isolated heads. No separate equipment layers.
Style: match the references' charming chunky BLACK AND WHITE pixel art exactly. Oversized head, compact short torso and legs, around 3.5 heads tall, front-facing neutral stance, hands down slightly away from hips, both feet visible. Same male face and spiky short dark hair throughout; same female face and shoulder-length wavy dark hair throughout. Keep faces friendly and readable, no realistic anatomy. Stepped square pixel contours, strong thick pixel outlines, large untextured white and black shapes. No smooth anime ink drawing, no elongated adult proportions, no gray, gradients, dithering, random dots, halftone, text, tiny intricate patterns, or realistic shading. Outfits must be recognizably DIFFERENT silhouettes, not mere recolors. Hats, mantles, wings and boots are integrated into the complete character.
This sheet is progression stage 1 of 10, outfit levels 1 through 10. Increase costume grandeur appropriately, ending in supreme celestial/divine armor, while preserving the same small friendly hero anatomy. ALL designs are original; no franchise logos, distinctive copied anime/film costumes or modern adaptation likenesses. Literary references use the original books as inspiration only.
Costumes A-J, in exact order:
A (Apprentice): plain white lace-neck tunic, dark trousers and simple boots.
B (Linen traveler): light rolled-sleeve linen tunic with broad dark belt.
C (Field scholar): short waistcoat, plain shirt, loose trousers and small journal pouch.
D (Book courier): short buttoned courier coat and a diagonal plain satchel strap.
E (Herbalist): simple apron over tunic, small leaf clasp and rolled sleeves.
F (Bookbinder): plain work apron and protective wrist cuffs, no tools held.
G (Forest scout): dark sleeveless vest, white shirt and light baggy trousers.
H (Ink scribe): short scholar robe with ink-drop brooch and dark sash.
I (Wayfarer): simple shoulder mantle, travel tunic and sturdy boots.
J (Novice guard): small smooth breastplate and plain rounded shoulder guards.
